ruxen 0.2.0: HTTP/2 for clients, HTTPS upstreams, client certificates, `auth_request`, and nginx's error pages, redirects and MIME types. ruxen is an experimental nginx-compatible HTTP server and reverse proxy written from scratch in Rust: Linux-only, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, thread-per-core on `io_uring` (monoio, epoll where `io_uring` is blocked), TLS via rustls.

> [!WARNING]
> This is an experimental release. It is not production-ready and is not a drop-in replacement for nginx.

This release closes the first part of phase 1 in [`ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/main/ROADMAP.md) (v0.2.0, "the essentials"): with a typical site's nginx configuration, ruxen can terminate TLS and HTTP/2, proxy to an application over HTTP or HTTPS, serve static files, and reload without dropping traffic. v0.3.0 is the rest of the edge: the proxy cache's remaining parts, cookie rewriting, variables in `root`.

## Security

- **A response whose write failed left no access-log line** (#410, low severity, CWE-778). A client that closed early, or a write that failed, was missing from the access log; nginx logs the request with the bytes it sent. Fixed in #412, with nginx's count of `$bytes_sent` for a response cut short (#413).

## Behaviour changes

- **`Content-Type` follows `types {}` and `default_type`**, as in nginx (#38). ruxen used to guess the type from a built-in table. A configuration that doesn't `include mime.types` now serves CSS and JavaScript as `text/plain` (or its `default_type`), as nginx does. The release tarball, the packages and the container image ship nginx's `mime.types` (`examples/mime.types`, `/etc/ruxen/mime.types`), and `examples/static.conf` includes it.
- **Built-in error responses are nginx's HTML pages** with `text/html` (#34); they were one line of `text/plain`.
- **Redirects to a path send an absolute `Location`** (`return 301 /path`, `rewrite … redirect`, directory redirects), as nginx's `absolute_redirect on` default does; `absolute_redirect`, `server_name_in_redirect` and `port_in_redirect` are honoured (#15).
- **Request headers to upstreams follow nginx's defaults** (#421): `Proxy-Authorization` and `Trailers` are forwarded, `Expect` is not.
- **`proxy_cache` keeps every variant of a response with `Vary`** (secondary keys, as nginx). Entries written by 0.1.3 miss once and are stored again.
- **Variable names are case-insensitive** (`$Host`, `${SSL_REDIRECT}` after `set $ssl_redirect`), and `$arg_*` matches the argument's name whatever its case, as in nginx (#459).
- **gzip of a response held whole is sent chunked over HTTP/1.1**, as nginx (the filter drops `Content-Length`); an empty body of a `GET` is compressed too. HTTP/1.0 keeps `Content-Length`.
- `ssl_protocols TLSv1 TLSv1.1 TLSv1.2` loads with a `[warn]` for the old names instead of failing (#36).
- `return 444` closes the connection without a response (#397). Plain HTTP on an `ssl` port gets nginx's 497 (#384).
- `SIGQUIT`: `worker_shutdown_timeout` ends the remaining connections, then the workers exit (#407).

## Install

Three prebuilt binaries, each also under a versioned name (`ruxen-v0.2.0-<target>.tar.gz`), with a `SHA256SUMS` file:

| tarball | for |
| --- | --- |
| `ruxen-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz` | x86_64 with glibc 2.35 or newer |
| `ruxen-aarch64-linux-gnu.tar.gz` | ARM64 with glibc 2.35 or newer (Graviton, Ampere, Raspberry Pi 5 on a 64-bit OS) |
| `ruxen-x86_64-linux-musl.tar.gz` | any x86_64 Linux, static (Alpine, older glibc) |

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/releases/download/v0.2.0/ruxen-v0.2.0-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS   # after downloading SHA256SUMS from this release
tar xzf ruxen-v0.2.0-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz
cd ruxen-v0.2.0-x86_64-linux-gnu
./ruxen -t -c "$PWD/examples/minimal.conf"
```

Container image, amd64 and arm64:

```bash
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/gvozdetsky/ruxen:0.2.0
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/
```

It runs as an unprivileged user. Docker's default seccomp profile blocks `io_uring`, so under it ruxen runs on epoll; [`contrib/docker/seccomp-io_uring.json`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.2.0/contrib/docker/seccomp-io_uring.json) allows `io_uring` and nothing else beyond the default (`--security-opt seccomp=contrib/docker/seccomp-io_uring.json`). A hardened systemd unit and a logrotate snippet are in [`contrib/`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/tree/v0.2.0/contrib).

From crates.io (needs `cmake` and a C compiler for rustls's `aws-lc-rs` backend):

```bash
cargo install ruxen --locked
```

## What's new since 0.1.3

### HTTP/2

- **HTTP/2 for clients** (#144): `http2 on;` and `listen … http2`, h2c with prior knowledge and ALPN `h2` per SNI, `$http2`, the `http2_*` directives (nginx's warnings for the obsolete ones), GOAWAY on keep-alive limits, shutdown and reload. Each stream goes through the HTTP/1.1 request path, so bodies, limits, trailers and `proxy_pass` work the same. `-V` claims `--with-http_v2_module`. Where the `h2` crate follows RFC 9113 and nginx doesn't (400 for malformed requests, a single GOAWAY, priorities): #347.

### TLS

- **Upstreams over TLS** (`proxy_pass https://`, #116): `proxy_ssl_server_name`, `proxy_ssl_name`, `proxy_ssl_session_reuse`, `proxy_ssl_protocols`, with nginx's defaults.
- **Upstream certificate verification** (#117): `proxy_ssl_verify`, `proxy_ssl_trusted_certificate`, `proxy_ssl_verify_depth`, `proxy_ssl_crl`, by OpenSSL's rules (AWS-LC's X.509 code: commonName fallback, depth, CRLs, `TRUSTED CERTIFICATE` blocks) and nginx's error-log lines.
- **Client certificates to upstreams** (#138): `proxy_ssl_certificate` / `proxy_ssl_certificate_key`, also with variables (#434), and `proxy_ssl_password_file`.
- **Client certificates from clients** (#113, #114): `ssl_verify_client` (`on`, `optional`, `optional_no_ca`), `ssl_client_certificate`, `ssl_trusted_certificate`, `ssl_verify_depth`, `ssl_crl`, the 400/495/496 pages, and `$ssl_client_verify`, `$ssl_client_cert`, `_raw_cert`, `_escaped_cert`, `_s_dn`, `_i_dn`, `_serial`, `_fingerprint`, `_v_start`, `_v_end`, `_v_remain`.
- **Encrypted keys**: `ssl_password_file` (#139).
- Each certificate, key, CA and CRL file is read once per configuration load, however many directives name it (a FIFO works), as nginx 1.27.2+.
- The next request on a TLS keep-alive connection is read directly (#145).

### Reverse proxy

- **`auth_request`** and `auth_request_set` (#358).
- **Responses are relayed as they arrive in nearly every case** (#88): gzip compresses a relayed body on the way, and an unframed HTTP/1.1 body ends with the connection. What is still read whole (a cache store, `add_trailer`, failover and interception): #463.
- **A client that goes away while the upstream is awaited ends the exchange with 499** (#136), as nginx.
- Ranges on proxied and cached responses: `proxy_force_ranges`, `max_ranges`, nginx's range filter (#370).
- `proxy_method`, `proxy_pass` inside `limit_except`, `proxy_cache_max_range_offset`.
- PROXY protocol v2: a family nginx doesn't know reads as `UNKNOWN`.
- `server 127.0.0.1;` in an upstream and `proxy_pass http://[::1]/` get the default port (#458).

### HTTP and configuration

- `types {}`, `default_type` (see above); a second `types {}` in the same block adds to the first, as nginx.
- `include` with patterns (`include conf.d/*.conf;`, #35).
- `add_header` and `add_trailer` at `http {}` (#17); `return URL;` (#16).
- Static files: several ranges as `multipart/byteranges`, nginx's range parse and 416 page (#401).
- `open_log_file_cache` for access-log paths with variables (#371); a request whose response the client doesn't take is logged (#410).
- **`docs/directives.md`**: every directive of nginx 1.24's core, events and http modules, and what ruxen does with it (#18). `ruxen --compat -c nginx.conf` checks a configuration against it.

### Running it

- A reload frees the retired configuration's memory (#343).

### Compatibility

- nginx-tests: 165 of the 191 files that apply pass (0.1.3: 105 of 159), see [`NGINX_TEST_PROGRESS.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/main/NGINX_TEST_PROGRESS.md).
- Config corpus: ruxen loads 217 of the 238 public configurations nginx accepts (91%; 0.1.3: 193), see [`corpus/RESULTS.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/main/corpus/RESULTS.md).

## Performance

- **Large responses are written as soon as they are read** (#247): a chunk of a file (`sendfile off`), of a relayed body or of TLS records goes to the socket at once, and only waits in `io_uring` when the socket is full. The write used to run at the next submit, after other connections had evicted the data from the CPU cache. On the i7: a 1 MiB static file with `sendfile off` 156% of main before the change (103% of nginx), a 1 MiB file over TLS 187%, relayed 64 KiB / 1 MiB bodies 105% / 108% (#469, #471, #472).
- The proxy's response-header scan and its pooled connections are lighter (#451, #462).

TBD: campaign on the release candidate, both machines.

## Known limitations

- No variables in `root` / `alias` (#232), no `proxy_cookie_*` (#40).
- A proxied body is still read whole in a few cases: a cache store, `add_trailer`, failover and interception (#463).
- No `proxy_request_buffering off` (#134), no runtime DNS (`resolver`, #133), no OCSP stapling (#141, #142).
- HTTP/2 to upstreams isn't implemented (phase 4 of the roadmap).
- With `sendfile on`, the file side of the transfer is synchronous; `sendfile_max_chunk` is not configurable.
- A reload can't bind new ports below 1024 after the switch to `user` (#344).
- `-V` reports `nginx version: nginx/1.29.2` (followed by `ruxen version: ruxen/0.2.0`): the nginx-tests harness reads that line and the `configure arguments` to decide which tests apply.

## How to help

- Found a config where nginx and ruxen behave differently, or one that ruxen refuses? Open an issue with the config, the request and both responses.
- Security problems: please report them privately, see [`SECURITY.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
- Setup, tests and benchmarks: [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
